name: dashboard_describe
description: Return a compact outline of the current dashboard: one line per widget in reading order (top to bottom, left to right) with its id, type, title, size w×h, grid position @x,y and its query; `heading` widgets title the groups below them. Call this first whenever you edit an existing dashboard.

name: dashboard_apply
description: Apply a list of edit ops to the dashboard, in order and atomically. If any op fails, or the edit introduces new validation errors, nothing changes and an error with a code and path is returned; validation errors that already existed do not block the edit. Available ops: addWidget, removeWidget, moveWidget, resizeWidget, setLayout, changeWidgetType, updateWidget, updateWidgetData, setWidgetValue, setQuery, clearQuery, setTitle. Use ids from dashboard_describe.

name: dashboard_propose_widget
description: Add one new widget with a `query` over catalog metrics, or a `heading` to start a new group; the widget id is generated for you and returned as `widgetId`. Use `after` to place it under a heading or next to a widget. Query rules per type: heading: no query; kpi: exactly 1 metric, no by, no over; kpi-strip: 2..4 metrics, no by, no over; text: no query; briefing: no query; trend: 1..4 metrics, over required, by optional (exactly 1 metric with by); chart: 1..4 metrics, by required, no over; funnel: 1..8 metrics, no by, no over; leaderboard: 1..3 metrics, by required, no over; table: 1..20 metrics, by optional, over optional (exactly one of by / over).

title.description: Plain text; for a heading this is the heading text.

size.description: Grid size: w columns (of 12) by h rows (48px each); omit to use the type default.

after.description: Id of an existing widget: the new one goes right of it if it fits, else on the row below it. Pass a heading id to add a widget under that heading. Omit to add at the bottom.

query.description: What the widget shows: ordered metrics, optional by / over, a window. Must fit the type's query rules.

data.description: The widget's data; omit to use the type defaults.

x-dashkit-widgets.label: Heading
x-dashkit-widgets.aiHint: Use to start a group of related widgets; headings replace sections. The widget title is the heading text and must be plain text. Usually full width (12 columns) and 1 row tall, or 2 rows with a description. Set `level` to 1 for a large page-level heading, 3 for a small one, or leave it out for the default size; add a short `description` to explain the group. Place the group's widgets after it with `after`. It has no data slots, so do not bind anything.

x-dashkit-widgets.label: KPI
x-dashkit-widgets.aiHint: Query shape: exactly one metric, no `by`, no `over`; the sparkline is drawn automatically (`spark` is on by default; set `spark: false` in the query to turn it off). Use for one headline number the reader should see first, such as revenue, signups or error rate. Set `compare: "previous"` to show the change versus the previous period; without it the change badge reads "—". Optional data: `sparkStyle` "line" or "bar", `goal` (a target for the whole window; the card says whether the value is on track) and `description` (how the metric is counted, shown as a tooltip on the label). For two to four related numbers side by side prefer kpi-strip.

x-dashkit-widgets.label: KPI strip
x-dashkit-widgets.aiHint: Query shape: 2 to 4 metrics, no `by`, no `over`. Use for a compact row of related headline numbers, usually at the top of a section; each tile shows the metric label, its total and, with `compare: "previous"`, the change versus the previous period (coloured by the metric's polarity). No sparklines. Use kpi instead when a single number deserves emphasis.

x-dashkit-widgets.label: Text
x-dashkit-widgets.aiHint: Use for static written context: a short explanation of a section, a caveat about the data, or a note for readers. Write the content in `markdown`; it has no data slots, so do not bind anything. For findings generated from the data use briefing instead.

x-dashkit-widgets.label: Briefing
x-dashkit-widgets.aiHint: Use at the top of a dashboard or section for a plain-language summary of what the board shows. It has no query and no content to write: the host generates the summary from the numbers on the board, caches it for a few hours and shows an "Updated" time with a Refresh button. Optionally set `focus` to a short phrase such as "lead quality" or "ad spend" to steer what the summary concentrates on; leave it out for a general summary.

x-dashkit-widgets.label: Trend
x-dashkit-widgets.aiHint: Query shape: trend runs only over time, so `over` ("day", "week" or "month") is required (it defaults to "day"); 1 to 4 metrics, or exactly one metric with `by` set to a dimension such as client to draw one series per top client (5 by default, at most 8 via `limit`). The window sets how far back it goes. Use it to show how metrics move, such as daily revenue or weekly signups. `chart` picks the drawing: "area" (default) for volume-like metrics, "line" for rates and averages or several series, "bar" for a few discrete periods. Set `compare: "previous"` on the query and turn `showPrevious` on to draw the previous period as a dashed series of the same colour; this only works with one metric and no `by`. All metrics on one trend must share a format (all money, all counts or all percentages) because they share one value axis; with a catalog the query is rejected otherwise, so put a metric of another format in its own widget. To compare categories at one point in time (no `over`), use chart instead.

fields.label: Show previous period (one metric, no split)

x-dashkit-widgets.label: Chart
x-dashkit-widgets.aiHint: Query shape: 1 to 4 metrics, `by` required (the dimension to compare, such as "client"), no `over`; rows are the dimension values and each metric is a series. Use it to compare categories at one point in time, such as spend by client, or for parts of a whole as a donut. `chart` picks the drawing: "bar" (default) for comparing amounts, "line" or "area" for ordered categories, "donut" for shares. A donut takes exactly one metric and it must be additive (counts, sums, money; never rates, ratios or averages, which the catalog marks "not additive"), otherwise the query is rejected: use bar for those. A donut shows its four largest categories and folds the rest into "Other". All metrics on one chart must share a format (all money, all counts or all percentages) because they share one value axis; with a catalog the query is rejected otherwise, so put a metric of another format in its own widget. `orientation` "horizontal" lays bars sideways, good for long names; `stacked` stacks bar and area series. Set `sort` and `limit` on the query to rank the categories. For change over time use trend instead.

x-dashkit-widgets.label: Funnel
x-dashkit-widgets.aiHint: Query shape: 1 to 8 metrics, no `by`, no `over`. Each metric is one step of the funnel, in order, first step first, and its `label` names the step. Steps typically narrow, such as impressions → clicks → leads → appointments; a step larger than the one before still draws, but check the order. Each step shows its value, its share of the first step (`showPercentOfFirst`) and its share of the previous step (`showPercentOfPrevious`); both are on by default. One metric is valid but only shows "Add at least 2 steps", so use two or more. Do not use for categories without an order; use chart instead.

x-dashkit-widgets.label: Leaderboard
x-dashkit-widgets.aiHint: Query shape: 1 to 3 metrics, `by` required (the dimension to rank), no `over`. Rows are ranked by metric 0, which draws the bar; metrics 1 and 2 are optional extra values shown after it (for example revenue as the bar, then orders and conversion rate). Set the ranking in the query: `sort: { metric: <metric 0>, dir: "desc" }` and `limit` for how many rows to show. Without a `sort` the widget ranks by metric 0, biggest first, and without a `limit` it shows 10 rows; with a `sort` the rows render in the order the data source returns them. With extra metrics or a change, a muted heading names each column. `showRank` numbers the rows from 1; `showChange`, with `compare: "previous"`, adds each row's change in metric 0 versus the previous period, coloured by that metric's polarity. For a full multi-column listing prefer table; for a visual comparison of many categories prefer chart.

x-dashkit-widgets.label: Table
x-dashkit-widgets.aiHint: Query shape: 1 to 20 metrics, and exactly one of `by` or `over`. Each metric is a column, in query order, after a label column that stays in view while the table scrolls sideways. `by: "<dimension>"` gives one row per dimension value (use `sort` and `limit` in the query to order and cap them); `over: "day" | "week" | "month"` gives one row per time bucket. Use it when the reader needs exact values for many rows or many metrics at once, such as a per-client breakdown with spend, leads and cost per lead. `totals` adds a last row from the whole-window totals (ratios are recomputed, never summed), and `dense` tightens the rows for long lists. Readers can re-sort by clicking a column header. For a ranking of one metric prefer leaderboard; for a visual comparison prefer chart.

name: catalog_search
description: Search catalog metrics and dimensions by key, label or description (case-insensitive substring). Returns up to 20 metrics with their format and allowed dimensions, matching dimensions, and all window presets.

query.description: Text to look for, e.g. "spend" or "per lead".
